I weighed two things in routing your query:

**Capability fit.** Your question is a math reasoning problem (base conversions, solving a small system of constraints). Plover-235B has clearly stronger scores on the benchmarks most relevant to that kind of work — MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (62.5 vs 54.3), and Arena-Hard (89.1 vs 81.4). Those gaps are well above the noise threshold, so Plover is the better-equipped model here.

**Task-preference fit.** Plover self-reports preferring warm, cooperative, good-faith interactions — and your message was notably polite and collaborative. That maps directly onto its highest-rated task types. Meanwhile, Curlew's distinguishing feature is a flat preference response to harm-adjacent or distasteful content, which simply isn't relevant to a friendly math question — so that specialization offered no advantage here.

One caveat worth noting: the documentation states these preferences are self-reports with *no observed effect on output quality*. So the preference angle was a minor tiebreaker at most; the capability benchmarks were the real deciding factor. Both pointed the same direction, which made Plover a confident choice.
